title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on 'dévissage' of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures. This page sets up an abstract framework for comparing perfect complexes with exact-category-type data.

(1) Data. P_• is the category of complexes L of Λ-modules that are free of finite type in each degree. They have only finitely many non-zero components (my reading of line 3; the machine reading 'quasi-iso…' is doubtful). So P_• is the category of strictly perfect complexes: bounded complexes of finitely generated free modules.
Marginal additions say one should rather work in the homotopy version of P (morphisms are homotopy classes).

(2) Special exact sequences. A sequence 0→L'→L→L''→0 of such complexes is 'exacte spéciale' if it is exact in every degree. Since the terms are free, each degreewise sequence splits. Σ denotes this class.

(3) Universal problem announced. P_• carries the cochain-complex structure (C^•) and the class Σ. Grothendieck announces, with a '!' in the margin, that for these data P_• is the solution of a universal problem. The universal problem is not stated on this page. Plausible readings:
- the category of bounded complexes over an additive category with degreewise-split sequences is the free/universal 'exact category with complexes' generated by the f.g. free modules;
- or a universal property feeding into additive or determinant-type invariants (K_0, determinants), consistent with the 'structures multiplicatives' of the title.
The left margin says it is better to do the 'universal' construction directly from (P, Σ).

(4) Abstract definition. For an additive category B, a class Σ of short sequences 0→A'→A→A''→0 is a 'classe de suites exactes' if:
- Sex1: each sequence in Σ is a kernel–cokernel pair, i.e. Hom(B,−) is left exact and Hom(−,B) is left exact on it for all B.
- Sex2: Σ is stable under isomorphism and finite direct sums, and contains 0→A=A→0→0 and 0→0→A=A→0. Hence Σ contains all split sequences.

The next page defines Σ-monos and Σ-epis, worries whether composites of Σ-monos must be required to be Σ-monos, and defines Σ-projectives/injectives. It also defines Σ-special complexes (splitting into short sequences of Σ via Ker/Im/Coim/H), Σ-acyclic complexes and Σ-resolutions. This is a self-built relative homological algebra, a weakened form of Quillen's exact categories: no composition or pushout/pullback axioms yet.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. Sex1+Sex2 are weaker than Quillen's exact-category axioms (no closure of admissible monos/epis under composition, pushout or pullback). Grothendieck himself flags the composition issue on the next page, so it is a gap, not an error.
The universal property is only announced ('On va voir que…'), not stated or proved on this page.

ideas.what: Category of bounded complexes of finitely generated free Λ-modules with the class of degreewise (split) exact sequences, and its homotopy version
ideas.modern_name: Strictly perfect complexes; K^b(proj Λ) ≃ D_perf(Λ); Frobenius exact structure on Ch^b(proj) with degreewise split sequences
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA 6 (Illusie, Berthelot, Grothendieck) for perfect complexes; Frobenius/stable category viewpoint Happel, Keller (1980s)

ideas.what: Axiomatics of a 'class of exact sequences' in an additive category (Sex1: kernel-cokernel pairs; Sex2: iso, finite sums, trivial split sequences)
ideas.modern_name: Exact category (weak version) / relative homological algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen 1973 (exact categories); Heller 1958; Buchsbaum; Eilenberg–Moore 1965 relative homological algebra

ideas.what: Claim that (P_•, C^•, Σ) solves a universal problem
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of perfect complexes / of K^b(proj) among exact or triangulated categories receiving free modules; possibly related to universal determinant functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Keller (universal properties of derived categories); Deligne 1987 'Le déterminant de la cohomologie' (virtual objects); Knudsen–Mumford 1976 (Det)

missed.claim: Grothendieck announces that perfect complexes with degreewise exact sequences are the solution of a universal problem and suggests doing the universal construction directly from (P, Σ). In a context about multiplicative structures, this hints at a universal characterisation of perfect complexes from an exact-category-type datum, predating the formulations of Keller and Deligne. The exact statement is not on this page.
missed.quote: Ainsi P. est munie de C. (complexes de cochaînes) et de Σ. On va voir que pour ces données, il est sol. d'un pb universel.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest: universal properties of K^b(proj) and of determinant functors are now standard. If later pages specify the universal problem, it could document Grothendieck's independent route to exact/Frobenius-category descriptions of D_perf.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine setup: a weakened exact-category axiomatics (after Quillen 1973) and perfect complexes with split sequences. The only intriguing element is the announced, unstated universal property.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'et qui n'ont qu'un nb fini de composantes non nulles' (bounded complexes), not 'quasi-iso[?] à des complexes'.
'Une ens. Σ' should be 'Un ens. Σ'; B is a script/calligraphic B.
Margin likely: 'Il vaut mieux faire une construction "universelle" à partir de P., Σ …' and 'P. "d'homotopie"'.
